newsitem.title: USA: U.S. consumer group urges reduction in debt levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. consumer group urges reduction in debt levels.

text.p: The Consumer Federation of America on Tuesday said a new study shows tens of millions of households were burdened with "significant" levels of credit card debt, and it urged both consumers and creditors to reduce debt levels substantially.
"Unlike auto and mortgage loans, most credit card debt has imposed costs, not benefits, on borrowers," said Stephen Brobeck, executive director of the federation, in a statement.
The group said its report showed consumers had charged more than $1 trillion on credit cards last year and that $835 billion of the charges were on four major credit cards.
Of that amount, it estimated that $374 billion to $396 billion was being "revolved" at the end of 1996, incurring interest obligations.
The federation made several suggestions for dealing with the problem, including urging creditors to show more restraint in the granting of revolving credit.
In most cases, the group said, creditors should not approve total credit lines greater than 20 percent of annual income.
The federation opposed legislative proposals by creditors that would restrict consumer access to Chapter 7 bankruptcy, where debts can be discharged.
